text:
ashwin: paging - seeing a spike of `KMS` API 500/503 and extreme latency from AWS KMS (us-east-1). Multiple services failing during startup because signing calls to KMS are timing out. Error spike started ~2026-03-15T02:10Z.

ashwin: example error from service-auth-prod logs:
```
2026-03-15T02:12:03Z ERROR signing failed: KMSException: 500 InternalServerError - requestId=abcd-1234
  at com.redwood.auth.SigningClient.sign(SigningClient.java:87)
  Caused by: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out
```

maria: ack. I'm looking at alerts + Grafana. KMS latency p95 jumped to 5s+, error rate ~18% for last 10m. This aligns with startup waves at ~02:10.

leo: adding context — we've seen transient KMS throttling before but not this long. Any account-wide maintenance or region event? aws-status shows no outages but there are elevated API errors in health events feed.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: KMS-dependency API latency/errors impacting startup and request signing. Severity: P1 (affects multiple services, customer impact). Pager escalation to oncall.

oncall-bot: paging oncall schedule: paging maria -> acknowledged. Next: leo (handoff planned).

maria: quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce fresh KMS calls during rolling restarts by enabling local signing cache for new pods if available, 2) increase client-side retries/backoff, 3) route non-essential traffic to fallback model. Starting 1) now for auth-service replicas.

ashwin: we have a Vault-backed ephemeral key fallback used for zero-downtime deploys. It's not enabled by default for all services. I can flip it on for auth-service only. TTL is 1h. Will coordinate with deployment.

maria: runbook step - set env `REDWOOD_KMS_FALLBACK=enabled` for `auth-service` in prod k8s deployment. Command: 
```
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/auth-service REDWOOD_KMS_FALLBACK=enabled
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/auth-service
```

leo: note: enable extra client retries on the signing client: `KMSClientConfig(maxRetries=10, backoff=exponential(200ms->5s))`. Will submit small config bump if we need to roll.

ashwin: toggled fallback for auth-service, rolling restart started. Monitoring logs.

maria: I'm also lowering our rollout concurrency for other services to avoid restart storm hitting KMS: setting `maxUnavailable` to 0 and staggering.

customer-ops: seeing a spike in auth errors from customers (500s) — CS queue is filling. Which tenants are impacted?

ashwin: initial list: customers with heavy startup patterns (batch workers) and some user logins. Not an auth DB issue — failing at signing. I'll produce a short customer impact blurb for CS.

maria: CS blurb (short): "We are experiencing elevated errors in our cryptographic signing dependency (cloud KMS) which is intermittently failing. We have enabled a temporary signing fallback for core auth services and are actively mitigating. We will provide updates when full service is restored." Feel free to paste.

incident-bot: update: mitigation (fallback) deployed to auth-service. Error rate for auth-service decreased to ~2% in the last 4m. Overall KMS API still elevated.

leo: can we route KMS calls through another region (us-west-2) as a stop-gap? There are cross-region latencies but might be better than 500s. Requires config change in client and potential IAM role allowed in that region.

maria: short answer: it's possible but not trivial. Service tokens are scoped to KMS key ARNs in us-east-1. We would need to provision a cross-region key and update key policy/roles. That will take >30m. Prefer to continue fallback + retries for now.

ashwin: I'm preparing a safelist so CS can whitelist affected tenants for manual workaround (reduce restarts). Also adding a metric tag `kms.fallback_active=true` to track which customers are served by fallback keys.

sre-bot: note: created a ticket to contact AWS support (case #CASE-20260315-1) with suspected KMS API degradation in us-east-1. Please attach logs/traces.

maria: action items now: (A) keep fallback enabled for auth-service until KMS stable (B) slide config retry up for signing client where safe (C) avoid mass restarts and stagger ops (D) contact AWS & monitor status. I'll stay on until stabilization and then hand off to night oncall.

leo: I'm going to prepare a safe partial region failover doc if AWS doesn't respond in 30m. Also check if GCP KMS could be used as a cross-cloud backup for certain non-customer-sensitive signing (requires more work).

ashwin: quick log after fallback: `2026-03-15T02:23:41 INFO signing using fallback vault key id=vault--ephemeral-xxx`. Auth-errors dropped ~85% for restarted pods.

customer-ops: pasted the CS blurb into Zendesk. Thanks.

incident-bot: update: AWS case opened. Ticket #CASE-20260315-1, severity escalated.

maria: status check @02:40Z - KMS error rate still elevated but trending down. Overall 5xx rate at 7% (was 18%). Latency p95 at ~1.2s. Continue monitoring.

leo: prepping handoff checklist for night oncall: what to monitor, runbook commands, who to escalate to at AWS.

maria: handoff plan: I'll stay until 03:30Z then hand to leo (oncall). Handoff notes: fallback is enabled on auth-service, rollout concurrency lowered, AWS case open, watch metric `kms.errors` and `auth.startup_failures`. Escalate to paging SRE lead if errors >10% for 20m.

ashwin: adding one more mitigation: opportunistic caching of service signing results (short-lived tokens) for 10m to reduce calls during surge. Implemented in auth-service runtime with feature flag `SIGN_CACHE_TTL=600`.

leo: thanks. If AWS responds with root cause (regional API backend) we'll publish final status. If they request traces, attach request ids from logs (I pulled a sample list).

maria: handing off now to leo (handoff_ts=1770124800). I'm going offline in 30m but will be reachable if needed.

leo: acknowledged. I'll take the night oncall. Current state summary for handoff message to SRE lead: "KMS API (us-east-1) had sustained elevated latency and 5xx starting ~02:10Z. Mitigations: enabled Vault fallback for auth-service, increased client retries, reduced rollout concurrency, added signing cache. AWS case opened. Error rates improving but still above baseline. Monitor and prepare region failover runbook if regression occurs."

incident-bot: note: please run the post-incident checklist once stabilized. Add task: reproduce failover test in staging and implement persistent cached keys for startup.

maria: agreed - postmortem items: 1) add reliable local key cache for startups, 2) implement cross-region key policy and test failover, 3) revisit KMS client defaults (retries/backoff), 4) add automated circuit-breaker that enables fallback when KMS error>threshold.

leo: accepted. I'll own the postmortem and schedule follow-ups. Leaving monitoring windows open.

customer-ops: CS updated customers with a timeline and ETA. Will update when we have clearer recovery time.

ashwin: final note before offline: we should add a short-term HLD doc for fallback keys so other teams can enable the pattern quickly. I'll draft one and link it in the incident doc.

maria: thanks everyone. Closing active mitigation thread for now, leave incident open until AWS confirms root cause.

leo: will update if anything changes.

sre-bot: incident status: mitigations applied. Postmortem owner assigned: leo. AWS case: CASE-20260315-1.

maria: signing off.

leo: 03:20Z - monitoring steady. last update from AWS: investigating API control plane in us-east-1.

ashwin: saved logs + request-ids to the case, uploaded traces.

incident-bot: last recorded message.
